title: waldsteinia fragarioides subsp. doniana
intro: Waldsteinia fragarioides subsp. doniana, commonly known as the creeping wood-sorrel, is a plant species in the Saxifragaceae family. It is a creeping perennial herb with leaves that resemble those of strawberries, and is native to Europe and Asia. The creeping wood-sorrel is valued for its medicinal properties, which include reducing inflammation and soothing digestive issues due to its health benefits, such as antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities. Its therapeutic actions include anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant properties, which are attributed to bioactive constituents like flavonoids and phenolic acids.
